 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING,
THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE E.S.INDIRESH  ORAL ORDER

In this writ petition, the petitioners are assailing the award dated 09.11.2023, passed by the respondent No.3 (Annexure-A), inter alia sought for writ of mandamus directing the respondent No.3 to recover and re-deposit the compensation from respondent Nos.4 to 7 and to consider the NC: 2024:KHC:45831 representation dated 31.01.2023 (Annexure-E) to the writ petition.

2. The relevant facts for adjudication of this writ petition are that, the petitioners' grandfather-Late Kempaiah, was the owner in possession of the land bearing Sy.No.66/3 to an extent of 35 Guntas and to an extent of 2 acres of land in Sy.No.221 of Obalapura Village, Thyamagondlu Hobli,
Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District.
It is contended in the writ petition that the writ petitioners are also the legal heirs of deceased Late Kempaiah, along with the private respondents herein.

Therefore, as the petitioners were not notified insofar as writ petition proceedings are concerned as well as passing of the award made by the respondent-KIADB and as it is the case of the petitioners that the petitioners are also entitled for compensation from the respondent-KIADB and as such, the petitioners have presented this writ petition challenging the award dated 09.11.2023 Smt Jayamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172479645/
3 (Annexure A).

sentences.text:
3. Heard Smt. Anitha N, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and Sri. Ravindranath B.,
learned Additional Government Advocate for respondent No.1, Sri. P. V. NC: 2024:KHC:45831 Chandrashekar, learned counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 3, Sri. Manmohan P N, learned counsel for respondent Nos.4 and 5 and Sri. S. G. Hegde, learned counsel for respondent Nos.6 and 7.
4.

It is contended by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners that, though the petitioners herein are also legal heirs of the original owner of land in question and without the consent of the petitioners, the respondent-KIADB, without considering representation made by the petitioners, has passed the impugned award dated 09.11.2023 (Annexure-A) under Section 29(1) of the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Act, 1966 and determined the compensation to be payable to the private respondents and therefore, sought for interference of this Court.

5. It is submitted by Sri.S G Hegde, learned counsel appearing for the private respondent Nos.6 and 7 that there is no impediment for identify the shares of petitioners as such and in this regard, he submitted that, the private respondents are ready to determine the compensation to be payable to the petitioners herein.
In the event, if their share has been made known to the respondents herein and therefore, he sought for NC: 2024:KHC:45831 dismissal of the writ petition.

In this regard, he filed a memo dated 29.10.2024 and submitted that, the respondent Nos.6 and 7 sought for disposal of writ petition keeping open the contentions of both the parties with regard to determine the compensation in terms of the memo dated 29.10.2024.
6.

It is also submitted by the learned counsel that, in view of the discussion held with the petitioners,
the respondents have agreed that they shall re-deposit a sum of Rs.26,35,416/- within two weeks from today towards the alleged share of the petitioners.
Therefore, the matter be referred to the Civil Court for further determination in the matter.

7. The submission made by the Sri.P. N. Manmohan, learned counsel appearing for the respondent Nos.4 and 5 that the respondent Nos.4 and 5 have compromised with the petitioners insofar as disbursement of amount is concerned.
Accordingly, he sought for bifurcation of the award amount to be payable to the petitioner and therefore, he sought for disposal of the writ petition.

Sri. P V Chandrashekar, learned counsel appearing for respondent-KIADB submitted that the compensation has been disbursed in favour of private respondent Nos.4 to 7 in terms of the award dated 09.11.2023 (Annexure-A) and further he submitted that as the respondent-KIADB has to pay approximately Rs.39,96,200/- to the petitioners as well as the respondent Nos.4 and 5 jointly,
which is the balance amount available with the KIADB.
Therefore, there is no impediment insofar as the amount, which is already paid insofar as the respondent Nos.4 to 7 is concerned.

Accordingly, he submitted that, in view of the lying of the amount as stated above with the KIADB is concerned, in the event if certain amount is being re-deposited by the private respondents, then the dispute be resolved and accordingly, sought for disposal of the writ petition.

sentences.text: In the light of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, on careful examination of the writ papers would indicate that the parties are agilating their rights insofar as the apportionment of compensation is concerned.

In that view of the matter, I am of the view that as the dispute has been raised by the legal heirs of the original owner-Late Kempaiah, insofar as the disbursal of the compensation is concerned, I am of the view that, the impugned consent award passed by the respondent-KIADB dated 09.11.2023 (Annexure-A) is to be set aside and the respondent-KIADB be directed to, refer the matter to the Civil Court for further action in the matter insofar as disbursal of compensation is concerned.
It is made clear that, it is the Civil Court alone is to determine the rights of the parties, in light of the observation made above.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed.
ii. In view of setting aside the consent award dated 09.11.2023 (Annexure-A), the private respondent Nos.4 to 7 are hereby directed to re-deposit the amount before the respondent No.3-KIADB.

In turn, the respondent-KIADB shall deposit the same before the Civil Court NC:
2024:KHC:45831 for adjudication with regard to the apportionment of compensation is concerned.
iii. The private respondents are directed to re- deposit the amount within a period of 2 months from the receipt of this order.

SD/-
(E.S.INDIRESH) JUDGE AMA Smt Jayamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172479645/
